terra.problem: Papa describes attending a family cookout, inventing an experience outside his established world and family story.
The text says Peter followed at a distance, not that he was behind a crowd or way back.
The passage does not establish that nobody tied Peter to anything or that he walked in by himself.
The text does not say nobody else in the courtyard had spoken or that the servant girl did not whisper.
The passage does not establish that Peter is not a worker in the high priest’s house.
The text does not say a stranger would not get a long look, or that the servant girl thinks she knows exactly who Peter is.
The explanation repeats Peter’s denial without adding anything, making it flat and generic.
The rooster crows while Peter is speaking, but the text does not say Peter never finishes his sentence.
The passage does not say the rooster’s crow interrupted Peter.
Saying the look says it all assigns meaning to Jesus’ look that the passage does not give.
Peter remembers the Lord’s words, but the text does not say he hears the denials play out in his head.
The explanation calls Peter’s response grief as a fact. His feeling should be marked as Papa’s guess.
The text says the council met at daybreak, not that they sat down.
The Sanhedrin is the council, not necessarily a council hall.
The explanation reveals that Pilate and Herod appear later, giving away what happens in the continuing story.
The explanation repeatedly restates that they will not believe without adding insight or personality.
After quoting Jesus, the explanation repeats the same point twice without adding insight or personality.
Jesus says they will not answer; the passage does not say they will be silent.
The text says they all ask, but it does not say they ask together at the same time.
